related_synthesis_entries.limit: The resulting proportions are lower bounds under the source's hypotheses, not exact nonvanishing densities.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: Positivity bounds mean central order, and root-number parity discretizes that bound into nonvanishing proportions; treating the two signs separately produces a strict gain that the parity-mixed orthogonal kernel cannot see.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The alpha_2 bounds control average central vanishing order in both large-weight and large-level sign families. Even order in the plus family and odd order in the minus family convert these bounds into proportions exceeding 9/16 and 15/16; combining the split families gives mean order strictly below one, whereas the O-kernel test gives only at most one. The analogous support-4/3 Sp argument gives symmetric-square nonvanishing exceeding 55/64.
directed.conceptual_reading: A continuous density inequality gains combinatorial force from parity: the allowed vanishing orders have gaps, so an average-cost bound controls the mass of exceptional forms.
directed.representation_or_bridge: The extremal kernel value is the bridge from one-level density to arithmetic proportions; sign splitting preserves information discarded by the mixed O representation.
directed.boundary_or_failure: These are conditional lower or upper bounds, not exact limiting proportions, and strictness depends on support beyond the diagonal plus nonconstant-kernel optimization.
directed.uncertainty: The inequality chain is intact, but exact fractions in the extraction should be checked against the scan before quotation.

supported: The alpha_2 bounds control average central order in both sign families; even/odd parity converts them into sharper arithmetic proportions.
The plus family has central nonvanishing proportion greater than 9/16, the minus family has order exactly one proportion greater than 15/16, and the combined mean order is strictly below one.
The analogous support-4/3 symplectic argument gives symmetric-square nonvanishing greater than 55/64.
inference: Describing parity gaps as converting an average-cost bound into control of exceptional mass accurately reflects the displayed inequalities.
paraphrase_or_style_risk: The spontaneous phrase 'nonvanishing proportions' blurs two different conclusions: odd-sign forms necessarily vanish centrally, so the 15/16 result concerns minimal order one (equivalently nonzero first derivative), not L(1/2,f) nonvanishing.
context_or_ocr_risk: Several numerical fractions are degraded in typography, although the inequality logic is intact.
missed_mechanism: The candidate should explicitly preserve the different target events for the two parities: order zero in the plus family versus order one in the minus family.
revision_instructions: Rewrite the parity consequence to say: plus-sign density bounds central nonvanishing, while minus-sign density bounds the proportion of simple central zeros/nonzero central derivative. Reserve 'nonvanishing' without qualification for the plus and symmetric-square cases.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: A projection argument characterizes when squared sinc is optimal
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Proves the Fredholm minimizer by decomposing any normalized competitor into the solution plus an orthogonal remainder, then shows the constant Fourier factor—and hence squared sinc—is optimal exactly when the kernel average is constant.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: For the SO kernels, symmetry reduces the Fredholm equation to explicit integral equations on half the interval, and trigonometric solutions turn qualitative nonoptimality of squared sinc into concrete improvements in nonvanishing and mean-order bounds.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: Evenness reduces the SO(even) and SO(odd) equations to integral equations on [0,1]. The source solves them by trigonometric functions, obtaining alpha_2 values approximately 0.8645 and 1.1145, then reports sharpened consequences approximately 0.5678 for plus-family nonvanishing, 0.94275 for minus-family minimal-order proportion, and 0.9895 for the combined mean-order bound.
directed.conceptual_reading: Solving the operator equation completes a chain from arithmetic off-diagonal terms to an adapted analytic probe and finally to quantitative arithmetic gains.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Even symmetry and differentiation or Fourier-series methods reduce the convolution equation to tractable trigonometric forms; the inner product with the solution gives the extremal value.
directed.boundary_or_failure: These optimized numbers remain consequences of the source's conditional density theorems, not exact nonvanishing densities, and this span does not safely expose every symmetry case in exact formula form.
directed.uncertainty: The construction and printed decimals are readable, but the extracted trigonometric formulas and cotangent arguments are garbled and should not be transcribed exactly without the scan.

supported: Evenness and uniqueness reduce the SO(even) and SO(odd) Fredholm equations to [0,1], and the source solves them with trigonometric/Fourier-series expressions.
The printed alpha_2 values 0.8645 and 1.1145 and the sharpened bounds 0.5678, 0.94275, and 0.9895 are present with their respective arithmetic meanings.
The candidate correctly avoids treating these conditional bounds as exact densities.
inference: The chain from an adapted kernel equation to quantitative gains is a faithful synthesis.
unsupported_or_imported: Differentiation is offered as a reduction method by the candidate but is not described in this span; the source names trigonometric functions/Fourier series.
context_or_ocr_risk: The exact trigonometric formulas and cotangent arguments are badly garbled; only the construction and printed decimals are safe without the scan.
revision_instructions: Remove the unsupported reference to differentiation and attribute the explicit solution only to the trigonometric/Fourier-series method stated in the span. Preserve the inequality directions when reporting the decimal consequences.
